title.narrative: Enhanced national capacity to implement SME policy and programmes and foster entrepreneurship, access to finance, formalization, green businesses and the social and solidarity economy

description.narrative:
Several factors weaken private sector development and decent work conditions in Iraq despite the availability of business opportunities and a number of economic reform plans. Among these challenges, it is worth mentioning lack of private sector and entrepreneurship culture, dependence on oil, highlighting limited economic diversification, weak governance and institutions, high public debt and security risks. The Decent Work Country Programme of Iraq aims at increasing the job creation potential of Micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in high-potential sector as well as enhancing MSMEs operating environment. While the ILO is engaged in supporting Iraq to improve the overall business environment for MSMEs and fostering private sector growth and development for decent job creation and will take action during this biennium to support informed policy discussions and reforms based on the assessment of the Enabling environment for sustainable enterprises that also looks at women-led enterprises.
The ILO is also exerting efforts to enhance the capacities of institutions to develop MSMEs support and entrepreneurship development programmes. The action under this track will cover access to financial services as well as trainings of financial and non-financial service providers.
